#### `impl ReadRecord for EventRecord`

```rust
impl ReadRecord for EventRecord
```

Reads one side of an event. `bin` is `EventRecord::bin`, and the typed readers come from the trait, so a
helper written against `&impl ReadRecord` works on either side of a merge as it does on a `Record`.
`generation` and `last_update_time` are zero on both sides of an `xdr-merge`.

#### `EventRecord`

```rust
pub struct EventRecord
```

One side of an event: a read-only record with its metadata. An `xdr-merge` handler is given two, the
record this cluster holds (`current`) and the write that arrived over XDR (`incoming`); see `event!`.

It reads like a `Record` - `bin`, `get`, `has` and the typed readers, with the same answers - and has
nothing that writes: a handler changes the record by what it returns (`Resolution`). Besides the bins it
answers what the server knows about its side of the merge: `is_delete` and
`is_partial` of the incoming write, `is_tombstone`
of the current record, and per bin when and by which DC it was written.

It is `Copy`, and valid until the handler returns. Its bins are read through the event's own import, never
the ordinary record natives, which in an event answer "nothing": a `Record` has no place in a handler.

#### `EventRecord::bin_names`


The names of the bins this side has, as a stored list of strings to iterate. Each is at most 15 bytes,

```rust

for name in incoming.bin_names().iter() {
    let name = name?;
    let name = name.as_str(&mut buf)?;
    // ...
}
```

#### `EventRecord::deleted_bins`

```rust

```

The names of the bins this side deleted, as a stored list of strings: for the incoming write, its

#### `EventRecord::bin_last_update_time`

```rust
pub fn bin_last_update_time(&self, name: &str) -> i64
```

When this side last wrote the bin, in milliseconds since the Citrusleaf epoch,
2010-01-01T00:00:00Z: Unix milliseconds minus 1 262 304 000 000. The server gives a time for every
bin of both sides, a bin this side deleted included. For a write that came from another cluster it
is the time that cluster shipped, or, where it shipped none, the time the write arrived here.

A bin this side neither has nor deleted has no time, and the answer is the record's
`last_update_time`, which in an `xdr-merge` is 0: the side that has
the bin is then the newer.


The source id of the DC that wrote the bin. The server gives one for every bin of both sides; for a
bin this side neither has nor deleted, the answer is this side's `source_id`.

#### `EventRecord::with_bins`

```rust
pub fn with_bins(&self, overrides: Map) -> Result<Map, Error>
```

A new record built from this one's bins with `overrides` on top: every bin of this record goes in
unless the map already has it. The bins travel by position, never through the guest. `overrides` is
the map returned, filled in; it is what goes into `Resolution::Record`.

This prefers one side, so a handler that uses it on `current` is not symmetric: the two DCs would
resolve the same pair to different records. `Pair::with_newer` is the symmetric form; use this one
when the side is chosen by something both DCs agree on, such as the source id.

```rust
let winner = if incoming.source_id() > current.source_id() { incoming } else { current };
let out = as_udf::map(1)?;

out.insert("merged", true)?;

Ok(Resolution::Record { bins: winner.with_bins(out)? })
```

Only bins this record has go in. A bin it deleted is not one of them (see
`deleted_bins`), so nothing deleted comes back.

#### `Pair`

```rust
pub struct Pair
```

The two sides of a merge, read bin by bin into a `Both`. Made by `Pair::of`.

A handler that merges some bins itself and leaves the rest to the last writer of each reads the
bins it knows through the pair and finishes with `with_newer`:

```rust
let pair = Pair::of(current, incoming);
let out = as_udf::map(2)?;

if let Some(visits) = pair.int("visits")?.max() {      // a counter that only grows
    out.insert("visits", visits)?;
}

if let Some(total) = pair.int("total")?.sum() {       // each DC's own share, added
    out.insert("total", total)?;
}

Ok(Resolution::Record { bins: pair.with_newer(out)? })
```

Each reader is the `EventRecord` reader of the same name asked of both sides. `Pair` is `Copy`.


The current record and the incoming write side by side, for bin-wise merging. Each record knows
which of the two it is, so the pair comes out the same if they are passed the other way round.

#### `Pair::with_newer`

```rust
pub fn with_newer(&self, overrides: Map) -> Result<Map, Error>
```

Every bin either side has that `overrides` lacks, from the side that wrote it later, so a handler
merges the bins it knows about and leaves the rest to the last writer of each. Symmetric: both DCs
order the two sides the same way.

`overrides` is the map returned, filled in, and is what goes into `Resolution::Record`. A bin
already in it is left as the handler set it. A bin that exists on one side only is taken from that
side, whichever wrote later - **unless the side that wrote later deleted it**: a bin named in the
newer side's `deleted_bins` is left out of the map, which deletes it, so
the older side's value does not bring a deleted bin back.

```rust
pub fn incoming_is_newer(&self, name: &str) -> bool
```

Whether the incoming side wrote the bin `name` later than the current side, per bin. The later
`bin_last_update_time` wins, and
on equal times the greater `bin_source_id`; see
`Both::incoming_is_newer`.

#### `Both`

```rust
pub struct Both<T> {
    pub current: Option<T>,
    pub incoming: Option<T>,
    // and private fields
}
```

A bin on both sides of a merge, either of which may be missing, with the merges a resolver reaches for.
Made by the readers of a `Pair`. `current` and `incoming` are the two values, `None` on a side that does
not have the bin; they are public for a merge that none of the methods covers.

```rust
let visits = pair.int("visits")?.max();             // Option<i64>: the larger
let total = pair.int("total")?.sum();               // Option<i64>: a missing side counts as 0
let name = pair.string("name")?.newer();            // Option<Text>: last writer wins

if let Some(visits) = visits {
    out.insert("visits", visits)?;
}
```

The methods take `self`: a `Both` is read once. The ones that return an `Option` give `None` only when
neither side has the bin.

#### `Both::incoming_is_newer`

```rust
pub fn incoming_is_newer(&self) -> bool
```

Whether the incoming side wrote this bin later: by the bin's last update time, and on a tie by
source id, so "newer" means the same on both DCs even when the clocks agreed to the millisecond.

Combine the two when both exist, as `f(current, incoming)`; the one that exists otherwise, without

#### `Both::sum`

```rust
pub fn sum(self) -> Option<i64>
```

The sum; the one that exists when only one side has the bin, a missing side counting as zero, and
`None` when neither does, as `max` and `min`. It wraps on overflow, as two's complement does, rather
than trapping. Adding the two sides is right only when each holds its own DC's share; summing two
copies of one counter counts twice.

#### `Both::sum`

```rust
pub fn sum(self) -> Option<f64>
```

The sum; the one that exists when only one side has the bin, and `None` when neither does, as `max`
and `min`. Right only when each side holds its own DC's share.

#### `Both::max_per_key`

```rust
pub fn max_per_key(self) -> Result<Option<Map>, Error>
```

`max_per_key` of a map bin on both sides, as `Pair::map` reads it: every key of either side, each
with the larger of its two integers. `Ok(None)` when neither side has the bin.

```rust
if let Some(counts) = pair.map("counts")?.max_per_key()? {
    out.insert("counts", &counts)?;
}
```

Symmetric, idempotent and associative, so the two clusters converge on the same bytes. For a `Both`
of maps: on one read with `Pair::list` it pairs up the elements.

`lww_by_version` of a `[version, value]` bin on both sides, as `Pair::list` reads it: the side

#### `max_per_key`

```rust
pub fn max_per_key(current: Option<Value<'_>>, incoming: Option<Value<'_>>) -> Result<Option<Map>, Error>
```

The per-key maximum of two maps: a new map with every key of either side, each under the larger of its
two values, or under its one value when only one side has the key. Built on the host, so it is ordered
by key and both clusters build the same bytes. `Ok(None)` when both sides are missing.

A side is `None`, or `Value::Nil`, when it is missing; otherwise it must be a map whose keys are
strings or integers and whose values are integers. Anything else is `Err(WrongType)`, a side that is not
a map included: a merge does not guess what a double or a nested map should become. `Err(Refused)` when
the host does not build the map.

```rust
let merged = as_udf::max_per_key(rec.get("seen")?, Some(theirs))?;
```

Symmetric (`max_per_key(a, b)` and `max_per_key(b, a)` are the same map), idempotent (merging a map
with itself, or with a merge it is part of, changes nothing) and associative (three sides merge to the
same map in any order): the laws a convergent merge needs. It is the merge of any map of values that
only grow; `counter_merge` is the same merge under the name of the structure it serves.

#### `sorted_union`

```rust
pub fn sorted_union(current: Option<Value<'_>>, incoming: Option<Value<'_>>) -> Result<Option<List>, Error>
```

The union of two lists as a set: a new list with every element of either side once, sorted, so both
clusters build the same bytes whatever order the elements arrived in. `Ok(None)` when both sides are
missing.

The elements are integers, strings or blobs: the kinds the server keys a map by, since the host sorts
them as a map built on it sorts its keys. Integers come first, by value, then strings and then blobs,
each by its bytes. An integer and a string are never the same element, however they read.

A side is `None`, or `Value::Nil`, when it is missing; otherwise it must be a list of those kinds.
Anything else is `Err(WrongType)`: a side that is not a list, or an element of another kind (a double, a
nested list or map, nil). `Err(Refused)` when the host does not build the list.

Symmetric, idempotent and associative: the merge of a set that only grows. A removal needs a second
set, as the 2P-Set of the CRDT tutorial keeps one.

#### `counter_merge`

```rust
pub fn counter_merge(current: Option<Value<'_>>, incoming: Option<Value<'_>>) -> Result<Option<Map>, Error>
```

The merge of a per-origin counter: a map of origin to count, each origin's count raised only by the
cluster it names, merged by the larger count per origin. It is `max_per_key` under the name of the
structure: the same rules, the same errors, and `Ok(None)` when both sides are missing.
`counter_total` reads the counter's value.

```rust
let counts = as_udf::counter_merge(current.get("hits")?, incoming.get("hits")?)?;
```

Symmetric, idempotent and associative. A count that goes down is not a count this merges: a
PN-Counter keeps a second counter for the decrements.

#### `counter_total`

```rust
pub fn counter_total(counter: Option<Value<'_>>) -> Result<i64, Error>
```

The value of a per-origin counter: the sum of its counts, wrapping on overflow. `Ok(0)` for a missing
counter (`None` or `Value::Nil`). `Err(WrongType)` when it is not a map, or when a key is not a string
or an integer or a count is not an integer, as for `counter_merge`.

```rust
let total = as_udf::counter_total(rec.get("hits")?)?;
```

#### `lww_by_version`

```rust
pub fn lww_by_version<'a>(current: Option<Value<'a>>, incoming: Option<Value<'a>>) -> Result<Option<Value<'a>>, Error>
```

Last writer wins by an application version: of two `[version, value]` lists, the one with the higher
version, as it is, to write back. Two equal versions are decided by the lists' stored bytes, the greater
winning, so both clusters pick the same side; two lists with the same bytes are the same either way.
`Ok(None)` when both sides are missing.

A side is `None`, or `Value::Nil`, when it is missing; otherwise it must be a list of exactly two
elements whose first is an integer (`Err(WrongType)` for anything else). The value may be of any kind.

```rust
// The write UDF moves the version and the value in one write: rec.set("price", &[version + 1, price]).
if let Some(price) = as_udf::lww_by_version(current.get("price")?, incoming.get("price")?)? {
    out.insert("price", price)?;
}
```

Symmetric, idempotent and associative: it is the larger of the two by version, then by bytes, which is
a total order. The version is the application's, raised by every write that changes the value, so no
clock decides.

#### `Resolution`

```rust
pub enum Resolution {
    /// Keep the current record; the incoming write is dropped.
    KeepLocal,
    /// Apply the incoming write whole, as if it had won every bin.
    TakeRemote,
    /// Do what the server would have done without the handler. A set bound to a handler never uses bin
    /// convergence, so this applies the incoming write, as [`Resolution::TakeRemote`] does.
    Policy,
    /// The final record is no record: it is removed on this cluster, leaving a durable tombstone so that a
    /// late write cannot bring it back. The delete is not shipped: the other cluster decides for itself,
    /// so a merge that deletes has to delete on both sides for the two to agree.
    Delete,
    /// The record is removed on this cluster outright, with no tombstone, so a later write creates it
    /// again. Like [`Resolution::Delete`], it is not shipped to the other cluster.
    Expunge,
    /// The final record: these bins, whole - a bin not in the map, or set to nil, is deleted. **At least
    /// one bin must be left**: a record of no bins is the handler's failure, not a deletion, so that a
    /// merge which built nothing by mistake does not remove what it merged. Say [`Resolution::Delete`]
    /// to remove the record.
    Record { bins: Map },
}
```

What an `xdr-merge` handler answers: which record this cluster ends up with. A handler returns
`Ok(resolution)`; an `Err` fails the merge with the error's message.

```rust
if incoming.is_delete() {
    return Ok(Resolution::TakeRemote);
}

let pair = Pair::of(current, incoming);
let out = as_udf::map(1)?;

out.insert("visits", pair.int("visits")?.max().unwrap_or(0))?;

Ok(Resolution::Record { bins: pair.with_newer(out)? })
```

A `Map` of bins converts to `Resolution::Record`, so `Ok(bins.into())` is enough.

A handler answers no time to live: the server gives the merged record the later of the two records'
expirations, and a record that never expires wins.
